title: Texas Cotton Down 15.8%. It's Giving Texarizona.

intro_meme.prompt: A cartoon weather-map character sweating bullets, arms flailing in panic, standing in front of a wall of red glowing drought icons, spotlighted like a stand-up stage.

outro_meme.prompt: The same sweating weather-map character now giving an exhausted thumbs up, pointing toward a glowing 'READ MORE' sign.

sources.fact: Texas cotton yield is forecast 15.8% below 2025 — nearly double the 9.0% national decline — with High Plains drought named as the main driver. 93% of Texas is in some stage of drought, and about 10% of the state's 3.7 million reported dryland crop acres had already been declared failed as of Sept 11, 2026.
USDA designated three Texas counties primary natural disaster areas on Sept 14, 2026, opening fast-track emergency credit, with additional contiguous counties made eligible.

lines.speaker: nate
lines.text: Kai, Texas cotton yield down fifteen point eight percent this year!

screen.prompt: A cartoon thermometer shaped like a cotton boll melting under a blazing sun, sweat pouring off it, a giant '-15.8%' stamped across it.

lines.voice_instructions: Channel Richard Pryor-style stand-up energy: exasperated, escalating, physically reactive delivery — real gasps, real disbelief, voice cracking on the big number. This is two friends losing it together over something absurd, not a news broadcast. Real cursing where the line calls for it, land every word of it like a punchline, not a warning label.
